result.title: TreePIN$^{2}$: Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks
result.summary: Fitted decision trees provide predictive knowledge for neural network initialization. We present Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks (TreePIN$^{2}$), a method that translates split rules, decision paths and leaf predictions into initial network weights and biases for classification and regression. Sigmoid units encode split responses, hidden units combine them along decision paths, and leaf predictions initialize the output layer. We calibrate split softness using local training margins, sample support and impurity reduction, relating the initial responses to the data at each node. All weights and biases remain trainable, allowing gradient-based optimization to refine the transferred decisions and their combinations. Across six classification and six regression tasks with twenty paired seeds, TreePIN$^{2}$ improves mean initial and early validation performance over initialization baselines on most tasks. After fifty epochs, it achieves the best or tied-best mean validation performance among the six compared methods on ten tasks. Paired ablations show how split calibration and leaf-informed output initialization contribute to the starting predictor and its subsequent learning.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 TreePIN²，把拟合决策树的分裂规则、决策路径与叶节点预测转换为神经网络的初始权重和偏置，并用局部训练间隔、样本支持度和不纯度下降校准分裂软度，随后允许梯度继续训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 把离散决策路径写成可训练的连续参数，可能为 LVR 中如何用显式推理结构初始化或约束 latent 状态提供线索，但论文面向表格分类与回归，与视觉证据、停止决策无直接关联，可供核查其结构先验的注入方式。
